land.text: Kuru country: 'from the Ganga and the Panchala border in the east to the Sarasvati and the Rohtak frontier in the west', 'Thanesar, Delhi, and most of the upper Gangetic Doab' (Kuru page), 'roughly corresponded to the modern Thanesar, state of Delhi, and Meerut district' (Mahajanapadas page); Hastinapura 'modern Meerut, Saharanpur, and Aligarh divisions'; the Panchala country is subtracted

successors.note: Same state under a new name and regime: the Kuru page has 'the Kurus ... switched to a republican form of government' by the Buddha's time (Kuru Ganasangha), and the Mahajanapadas page dates the switch to 'the 6th to 5th centuries BCE'. The sa-01-b dossier starts in -600 with Cliopatria's Mahajanapada row; rule 2 of the map (one colour per state) applies to the pair.

capitals.name: Hastinapura (Meerut district)
capitals.note: The page lists three seats without years: Asandivat (modern Assandh, Haryana), Hastinapura and Indraprastha (Purana Qila, Delhi); it calls Hastinapura and Indraprastha 'the main later Kuru cities' and says post-Vedic sources move the capital to Kaushambi after Hastinapura was flooded (semi-legendary). The span is the state's life; the order of the seats is not on the page. Coordinates are the site's (the page gives none).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Vedic Kuru; its Janapada of Kuru row begins in -600 as two 5,232 km2 discs on Delhi, which the sa-01-b dossier widens to about 15,600 km2). The page gives no area; the shape resolves to about 52,000 km2, the 'upper Gangetic Doab' plus the Thanesar and Delhi country the page names. Larger than the Mahajanapada-era Kuru because the page says the earlier kingdom was 'dominant roughly from 1200 to 800 BCE' and 'by the 5th century ... a backwater'.

ledger.note: c. 1200 BCE: the Kuru kingdom forms from the Bharata and Puru tribes. 'The kingdom formed in the Middle Vedic period (c. 1200 to c. 900 BCE) from the alliance and merger of the Bharata and Puru tribes', 'dominant roughly from 1200 to 800 BCE', with Parikshit and Janamejaya as the rulers of its rise. The infobox says 'c. 1900 BCE - c. 345 BCE', which the body does not support; the year is the body's, the country is the page's bounds.

region.text: Kuru country: 'from the Ganga and the Panchala border in the east to the Sarasvati and the Rohtak frontier in the west', 'Thanesar, Delhi, and most of the upper Gangetic Doab' (Kuru page), 'roughly corresponded to the modern Thanesar, state of Delhi, and Meerut district' (Mahajanapadas page); Hastinapura 'modern Meerut, Saharanpur, and Aligarh divisions'; the Panchala country is subtracted

ledger.note: c. 600 BCE: the Kuru monarchy becomes the Mahajanapada of Kuru. The Mahajanapadas page has the Kurus, 'a well known monarchical people in the earlier period', switching 'to a republican form of government during the 6th to 5th centuries BCE'; the Kuru page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuru_Kingdom) has Kuru 'something of a backwater' in the 5th century, 'a minor state ruled by a chieftain named Koravya'. -601 is the year before the Mahajanapada convention year (-600); neither page gives a year for the change.

wars.name: Kurukshetra War (epic conflict between two branches of the Kuru clan)
wars.outcome: No territorial result: the Kuru page says the epic 'describes a conflict between two branches of the Kuru clan, possibly around 1000 BCE. Archaeology hasn't confirmed the events.'
wars.note: Listed so the reviewer can see it was considered; the text of the Mahabharata 'mostly dates to c. 400 BCE-400 CE'. Not drawn.

certainty.note: A Vedic kingdom known from texts; the page's bounds are rivers and towns, its dates are 'c.' dates and the infobox contradicts the body.

sources.title: Kuru Kingdom
sources.note: Formation c. 1200-900, dominance 1200-800, decline by 500, extent 'Thanesar, Delhi, and most of the upper Gangetic Doab', Hastinapura and Indraprastha, correspondence with Painted Grey Ware, Kuru Ganasangha.

sources.title: Mahajanapadas
sources.note: The Kuru country 'roughly corresponded to the modern Thanesar, state of Delhi, and Meerut district'; the Kurus' republican switch in the 6th-5th centuries BCE; the Mahajanapadas dated 'sixth to fourth centuries BCE'.

notes: Written from the group scope's 'Vedic janapadas before 600 BCE'; sa-01-b's janapada-of-kuru begins in -600 and lists no predecessor, so it should name kuru-kingdom (the two are one state: same hue, rule 2). Overlap: the Painted Grey Ware culture (this batch) covers the same country, and the Kuru page says the kingdom 'corresponds with the archaeological Painted Grey Ware culture'; the renderer should let the state win over the culture. The page's infobox dates (c. 1900 BCE - c. 345 BCE) conflict with its body (c. 1200 formation) and are not used. No territorial event is dated between 1200 and 600 on the two pages, so the shape is constant; the Kuru-Panchala relation (Kesin Dalbhya, a Panchala king, took over leadership after the Kuru king died) is not a transfer of land. Gazetteer: Hastinapura (29.17N 78.02E) and Assandh are not places.
